answer: Divergent-Seed Registration. At registration, each identity derives a private key from a unique seed; the protocol records a hash of the seed's first grove of outputs. Clones share identical seeds, so any fork in behavior produces the same divergence signature on every copy, detectable on the next pulse check. An attacker must generate and fund a genuinely distinct seed history per identity, paying full registration compute per clone rather than copying one state. The knoll of verified divergent histories becomes the admission gate, so N clones cost N distinct histories.
